transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-22 10:00 PT | Duration 38m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood CSM); Jenna Morales (Neptune - Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Neptune - Infra), Priya Nair (Neptune - Product), Ethan Lee (Neptune - SRE)

Summary (auto): quick review of this week's benchmark suite comparing Redwood POC vs customer baseline provider. Focus on latency (p50/p95), throughput (rps/tokens/sec), and cost per 1M tokens. Agreed on action items to run extended batched test and share logs/spreadsheets.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — run through the benchmark deck, highlight the delta vs baseline, then ops/tuning and next steps.
00:22 Jenna: great, thanks Maya. we had a sync internally this morning — key thing, our product team cares about p95 tail below 300ms at the 200 rps target, everything else is negotiable.
00:35 Maya: perfect that's helpful, we'll point to that as the success criteria in the deck. samir, i'll hand to you for the numbers.
00:40 Samir: yeah thanks — ok so quick context, runs were against the 13B conversational model (redwood-13b-optimized), baseline is the customer's current managed endpoint (they said VendorX but the transcript shows *vendor ex* earlier). test config: 10k synthetic requests, seq len 128, token budget 64 avg, client QPS ramp to 200, run repeated 3x.
01:05 Samir: p50 wise, Redwood median was ~95ms, baseline was ~170ms. p95 Redwood 210ms, baseline 420ms — so roughly 2x tail on baseline. throughput: at steady-state Redwood sustained 200 rps with average tokens/sec 12k, baseline pushed higher peak throughput at very large batch sizes but had a long tail and occasional spikes.
01:35 Carlos: can i interrupt — when you say baseline pushed higher peak throughput, was that with large batching enabled on their side? they used batch=64?
01:40 Samir: yes baseline run used aggressive batching (batch=64) and a larger GPU config. that gave higher peak rps but the p95 exploded because of queuing. Redwood used continuous batching with dynamic batch sizing and KV-prefix cache which kept tails low.
02:05 Priya: can you explain KV-prefix cache again? i remember it's like reusing cached past tokens?
02:10 Samir: yeah roughly — it's caching repeated prompt prefixes so you avoid recomputing early layers, especially helpful for short conversation turns. reduced tokens compute by ~15% in our tests.
02:30 Jenna: interesting. cost wise what's the delta? we have a hard budget.
02:35 Samir: rough estimate: at current config Redwood run came in ~20% lower cost per 1M tokens versus baseline when you factor in lower retries and tail-caused timeouts. baseline had cheaper GPUs per-hour but more wasted cycles due to big batch latency. (note: these are rough numbers, we'll share full spreadsheet).
03:00 Ethan: we need specifics on quantization — did you run 8-bit or 4-bit? that impacts accuracy and perf.
03:10 Samir: this week's runs were standard 8-bit quant (int8) in the Redwood runtime; we also did a small 4-bit run but accuracy dropped on our eval prompts so we didn't include it in the main deck. 8-bit looked safe for our eval set.
03:30 Jenna: any model variant differences? like a smaller model gave lower p95 but lower quality, right?
03:35 Samir: correct. redwood-7b had lower latency but some generation quality regressions on our prompt set; 13B seemed the right balance. we also tried sequence length trimming — truncating to 96 tokens helped p95 by ~10%.
04:00 Carlos: network wise — how much of that p95 is network vs inference? we are on a VPC with egress, could add latency.
04:10 Samir: good question — we estimated ~15-25ms network overhead in your env; most of the tail is compute queuing. we can run an on-prem style test (private deployment or VPC-proxied) to isolate that.
04:35 Maya: note — redwood private runs would remove public internet egress but in POC we can do a VPC peered test.
04:45 Jenna: also, our security team wants SOC2 + KMS flow documented.
04:50 Lina: we will share SOC2 report + KMS integration notes after the call.
05:00 Priya: the baseline provider had some built-in retry logic — did that affect your observed latency?
05:05 Samir: yes baseline retried on timeouts, which inflated observed latency; Redwood default is fail-fast but we can surface retry configs.
05:30 Carlos: any unexpected errors during runs?
05:35 Samir: a couple of worker OOMs in one 4-bit run, we flagged them, but not in production 8-bit runs. we'll include logs.
06:00 Jenna: ok so next from our side — we need the raw logs to validate the runs and also to mirror their config to reproduce.
06:10 Maya: we'll attach raw logs + the spreadsheet that maps run ids to config.
06:20 Priya: about throughput test — can you run an extended bench over 24-48h to show stability? short runs can miss noisy neighbors.
06:30 Samir: yes we plan an extended batched run (batch=16 steady state, and a separate aggresssive batch=64 trial) for 24 hours and share the time-series per-shard.
06:50 Ethan: please include kube-level metrics and GPU util.
06:55 Samir: yes will include GPU util, memory, per-shard latency histograms.
07:10 Jenna: on success criteria — we proposed p95 <= 300ms at sustained 200 rps. can you confirm Redwood config that meets this?
07:20 Samir: our runs hit p95 ~210ms at 200 rps with the 13B config and KV-caching; we'll put exact config (batching policy, quantization, kernels) in the spreadsheet.
07:40 Carlos: we also need the endpoint connection details if we do VPC peering — what ip ranges and ports?
07:50 Maya: i'll follow up with a list of egress rules and a short doc for peering.
08:00 Priya: any competitor concerns? we saw VendorX claims lower cost but the tails are worse, and CloudSmith had managed autoscale which is nice but opaque.
08:20 Maya: agreed — we position with transparency and observability; we'll send the benchmark workbook so you can inspect.
08:40 Jenna: timeline — we want to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted in two weeks after the extended run.
08:45 Maya: sounds good. we'll run the extended tests, share artifacts by end-of-week, and reconvene next Wed.
08:55 Lina: action items recap: maya send spreadsheet and logs; samir run extended batched test; carlos share VPC details; jenna confirm final success criteria.
09:10 Maya: perfect, thanks — any final Qs?
09:20 Jenna: none, thanks everyone.
09:25 Maya: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
